articleTitle: PCF Based Sensor: Detecting Nicotine in Smoke to Identify Cigarette Smoke in the THz Regime
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel gas sensor employing Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF) to detect nicotine found in cigarette smoke in the THz Frequency range. The optimization of this PCF involves adjusting various parameters such as shifting the core diameter, altering the pitch and diameter of cladding air holes, and modifying the background materials. This optimization process likely aims to achieve desired characteristics or performance outcomes within the photonic crystal fiber structure. This particular model enhances its sensitivity in detecting nicotine by effectively reducing confinement loss. We conduct a comprehensive numerical analysis to showcase its impressive performance across a range of optical parameters including refractive index, confinement loss, power fraction, and effective mode area. To evaluate its functionality within the 0.4 to 1.4 THz frequency range, we utilize the Finite Element Method (FEM) for our investigations. At 1 THz, 94.56% sensitivity is attained, in addition to the fact that the confinement loss is 1.91 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">⁻18</sup> dB/cm.

articleTitle: Waveform Design and Performance Analysis of DFT-Spread WR-OCDM System for PAPR and OOBE Reduction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Recently, orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) system has been proposed as an alternative waveform contender for next-generation wireless communication systems. OCDM is a spread spectrum (SS) technique that uses a set of orthogonal chirps as carriers for maximizing the spectral efficiency (SE). However, like OFDM, the OCDM system suffers due to its high out-of-band emissions (OOBE) and high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). These lead to adjacent channel interference (ACI) and signal degradation in transmissions. To solve these serious issues, we proposed an advanced OCDM system for reducing OOBE and PAPR without degrading communication quality. The proposed scheme combines discrete Fourier transform (DFT) precoding and time-domain windowing techniques along with the OCDM system. By DFT operation, the energy of each chirp of the OCDM system spreads over all the chirps. Hence, PAPR of the OCDM system is reduced. On the other hand, to reduce the OOBE of OCDM system, time-domain windowing is applied at the transmitter side. Simulation results verify that the proposed scheme reduces PAPR at the CCDF level of 1 × 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>by 2.43 dB compared to the conventional OFDM, OCDM, and windowing and restructuring (WR)-OCDM systems. In addition, the proposed scheme reduces OOBE by a maximum of 67 dB compared to the OFDM and OCDM systems. Moreover, the bit error rate (BER) performance is evaluated for different modulation formats, such as 4-QAM, 16-QAM, and 64-QAM over the AWGN channel. Our proposed system shows similar BER performance to the conventional multicarrier systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Implementation of the Ghost Polarimetry with a Spatial Light Modulator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The paper proposes a scheme of classical ghost polarimetry using a spatial light modulator to create structured patterns. Reconstruction of images and azimuths of anisotropy of objects with different distributions of polarization properties is presented. It is shown that the polarization pictures of objects with linear polarization of 0, 45 and 90 degrees are restored with great accuracy.

articleTitle: Eye-Shaped Labyrinth Metamaterial Absorber For C, X, Ku & K-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In the microwave frequency domain, this paper introduces a simple design aimed at designing a multi-band polarization-insensitive MA. Polarization-insensitive MA are currently highly appealing owing to their distinctive absorption characteristics across various polarization angles. This design involves imprinting a specific structure onto a metal-backed dielectric substrate FR-4, which comprises an eye-shaped labyrinth structure. Upon conducting a series of diverse analyses at an angle of incidence perpendicular to the surface, it has been determined that the proposed arrangement exhibits significant levels of absorption, reaching 94.93% at frequencies of 5.76 GHz, 97.73% at frequencies of 7.432 GHz, 95.89% at frequencies of 10.644 GHz, 98.28% at frequencies of 13.813 GHz, 93.18% at frequencies of 19.048 GHz, 98.72% at frequencies of 21.006 GHz, 99.9% at frequencies of 22.856 GHz, 91.85% at frequencies of 23.756 GHz, and 99.15% at frequencies of 24.746 GHz. To gain deeper insights into the absorption mechanism intrinsic to this design, provide visualizations of surface current distributions.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Different Shaped DRA Arrays for 70 GHz Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This paper presents four different shaped dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) arrays for the 70 GHz band suitable for millimeter wave (mm-wave) applications. Four 2×2 DRA arrays with rectangular, cylindrical, hexagonal and hemispherical shapes are designed and simulated using a low-cost silicon wafer with ɛ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 11.9 as the dielectric material. Proposed DRA arrays are compared based on variations in realized gain, 2D and 3D radiation pattern, beam steering capacity, etc. CST microwave studio software is used to simulate the DRA arrays. Realized gains of 13.3 dBi, 13.6 dBi, 13.6 dBi and 13.2 dBi, and beam steering of ±28°, ±27°, ±28° and ±27° are achieved at 70 GHz frequency for the rectangular, cylindrical, hexagonal and hemispherical shaped DRA arrays respectively. An approach to reduce the design complexity of System-on-Chip (SoC) integration has been made by proposing noble single silicon-based micromachined DRA arrays with coplanar waveguide (CPW) feeding mechanism discarding the need for additional substrate layers.

articleTitle: Enhanced Optical, Dielectric and Photocatalytic Properties of SR, CR Co-Doped BiFeO3 Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this work, BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (BFO) nanoparticles doped with Sr and Cr were synthesized following the sol-gel process. The effect of co-doping on the structural, morphological, optical, dielectric, and photocatalytic properties were studied. The X-ray diffraction data shows a distorted perovskite structure with maximum purity for the nominal composition Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.95</inf>Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.99</inf>Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.01</inf> O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. With increasing concentration of Sr and Cr content in BFO, particle size, optical band gap and dielectric constant decreases. The photocatalytic degradation efficiency of methylene blue dye using Sr and Cr co-doped BFO is higher than that of other BFO-based materials.

articleTitle: TA-PDP: An Topology Aware Partial Dominant Pruning Broadcast Protocol to Minimize Forwarding for Wireless Ad-hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Broadcast protocol is an essential part of wireless ad-hoc networks for fundamental network operations, route discovery, service discovery and even actual data transmission. Reducing number of forwarding stations is the main objective of a scalable broadcast protocol. Partial dominant pruning (PDP), a neighbor knowledge-based proactive approach, is an effective broadcast protocol for minimizing number of forwarding stations over legacy dominant pruning (DP). When two or more candidate stations cover same number of uncovered stations, PDP selects a station with smallest ID as a forwarding station. However, station ID do not give any contribution to reduce the number of forwarding stations as station IDs do not contain any topological information of the network. To address these issues, we develop a broadcast protocol named topology aware partial dominant pruning (TA-PDP) that uses neighbor information of candidate stations and selects a station with maximum number of one-hop neighbors and thus it reduces the number of forwarding stations. The simulation results show that the proposed TAPDP broadcast protocol outperforms DP and PDP in terms of number of forwarding stations, saved rebroadcast, redundancy, and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Dual-Circle with Quadrilateral-Split Ring Shaped Incident-Angle Insensitive EM Metamaterial Absorber for X and Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this paper, a quadrilateral-shaped structure for X and Ku band applications has been constructed using a combination of two circular and four quadrilateral rotational split ring resonators. With a FR4 substrate and a subwavelength dimension of 0.26λ×0.26λ, the unit cell functions as a single negative (SNG) absorber. The anticipated unit cell's enhanced effective medium ratio (EMR) provides indication of the MMA's compactness. This distinctive absorber is both phi (up to 180) and theta (up to 90) polarization insensitive and can absorb 93.70% to 99.99% of EM waves in transverse electromagnetic mode (TEM) at 8.57 GHz, 10.53 GHz, 11.17 GHz, 12 GHz, and 16 GHz frequencies. The established metamaterial absorber has promising future applications in anti-radar coating, automotive radar stealth technology, EMI shielding, satellite communication systems, radio astronomy and medical imaging.

articleTitle: Design of an Artificial Magnetic Conductor for C-and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: A dual-band zero-reflection phased artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) having a circular split ring resonator (CSRR) and cross-shaped structure is proposed for wireless applications. The suggested AMC resonates at 6.01 GHz and 10.08 GHz under normal and oblique incidence. The polarization conversion ratio (PCR) is almost unit at 6.01 GHz and almost 90% at 5.93-6.12 GHz, 10.92-11.68 GHz. Moreover, the AMC has a zero-reflection phase at 6.01 GHz, 7.14 GHz, 10.68 GHz, and 13 GHz. In addition, the 2×2 array of AMC unit cell is also designed for optimum performance. The PCR is approximately unit at 6.01 GHz and nearly 90% at 5.93-6.12 GHz, 10.92-11.68 GHz. Furthermore, the 2×2 array has also zero reflection phase at 5.46, 6.01, 7.12, 10.6 and 12.845 GHz. The electrical size of the AMC unit cell is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.31\lambda_{0}\times 0.31\lambda_{0}$</tex>. So, the suggested AMC can be used for meta-surface, gain enhancement purpose, wireless power transfer and for other C- and X-band wireless applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Network Lifetime of LEACH and LEACH-C for Free Space and Multipath Propagation by Varying Radio Energy Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: To attain peak performance throughout a wireless system's lifespan, Low Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH) merges the concepts of media access with energy-efficient clustering-based data transmission protocols. An optimization and more robust simulation known as Centralized LEACH (LEACH-C) is a modification of LEACH to ensure optimization and reduce information loss. We used the information about the node's placement and average energy in this centralized protocol which is called LEACH-C. We have presented the comparison of the lifetime of LEACH and LEACH-C using MATLAB simulation. The motive of this research is how the data rate, operating frequency, and antenna heights affected the network lifetime of LEACH and LEACH-C. Results from rigorous simulation conclude that the network lifetime of LEACH-C is 5.78% better than that of LEACH in the case of 914 kHz frequency and 1 Mbps bit rate of sensor node transmitter and antenna is 1.5 m above the ground. The last section of methodology and result show that, in the case of parameters of node transmitter defined in IEEE standard 802.15.4, the new frequency and bit rate affects the lifetime, energy consumption of LEACH and LEACH.

articleTitle: Mitigation of CD, PMD and Nonlinearity in Ultra High Speed Long Haul QAM-16 Coherent Fiber-Optic Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The impacts of chromatic dispersion (CD), polarization mode dispersion (PMD), and nonlinearity have become very significant for ultra-high speed long-haul fiber-optic communication systems. We are considering a system with 160 km long fiber having a speed of 112 Gb/s employing QAM-16. This paper addresses the above challenges, focusing on the mitigation of PMD, a stochastic impairment caused by differential signal polarization propagation. We have employed a simulation-based methodology following the OCSim module to simulate the transmission system with these impairments. Furthermore, we have incorporated the Constant Modulus Algorithm (CMA), a popular adaptive equalization technique for PMD compensation, and a systematic dispersion management system. Our findings reveal a complex interplay between the CD, PMD, and nonlinearity. We have generally observed an increase in the BER due to CD, PMD, and nonlinearity. However, we demonstrate that it is possible to mitigate these effects by optimizing the system parameters and applying the CMA algorithm, Frequency-Domain Equalizer, and digital post-processing technique. Thereby, the system performance can be improved.

articleTitle: The Study of Optical Properties for Ordered and Disordered Silicon Nanowire Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: We designed ordered and disordered silicon (Si) nanowire structures and analyzed their optical performance using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. We studied the orderness of nanowire structures by calculating scalar variance. This study reveals that utilizing disorder structures can increase the average absorbance of Si nanowire structures. Spatial electric field distributions provided insights into light-matter interaction, indicating that disorder structures had higher path lengths compared to the periodic structure. We achieved an average absorbance of 41.46% for the hyperuniform Si nanowire structure with a maximum absorbance of 78.18%. Intuitively, we obtained ~70 % high absorbance compared to periodic Si nanowire structure. Our findings will be conducive to designing new efficient solar cells and photodetectors.

articleTitle: Investigation of An Elliptic Terahertz Absorber Based On Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this research article, we show a tunable broad- band absorber based on a simple elliptic structure using vanadium dioxide at terahertz frequencies. We use a single elliptic resonator ring which is made of vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), positioned on top of a layer of metal and separated by a dielectric spacer. Through full vector numerical simulation, we calculate the absorption bandwidth in the given range, achieving nearly complete absorption (100%) throughout the span of frequencies from 3.5 THz to 4.7 THz. Our theoretical analysis reveals that modifying the ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta$</tex> of the semimajor and semiminor axis of the ellipse changes the absorption peak intensity and operating bandwidth as well. The proposed structure also experiences a change in the radii of the semimajor axis which eventually results in a change in the absorption rate. Because of the conductivity of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> that controls the properties of the substance, also responsible for the enhancement of the intensity of absorption. Interestingly, we observe that varying the incident angle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex>, modifies the absorption magnitude within the asymmetric structure. The distinct reliance on the angle of incidence offers possibilities for applications in the progress of sensing and imaging technology.

articleTitle: Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Based Ultra-Wideband Filters in Terahertz Region: A Finite Element Method Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Conventional electrical waveguides have become a major obstacle in future high frequency ultra fast data transmission. These traditional electrical micro-stripe lines suffer from low transmission, high insertion loss, and total reflection of the excitation signal at terahertz range. The Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton (SSPP) based waveguide can be a better alternative with low loss and tight field confinement within the metal-dielectric interfaces. This article investigates the transmission characteristics of a single SSPP waveguide filter with uniform corrugation on both sides of the metal line. Additionally, the effect of geometric parameters of SSPP filter on transmission coefficients (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) and reflection coefficients (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) has been investigated. The proposed SSPP model is simulated with six different design parameter values. Among them, the best performance is obtained with groove width 3 µm, height 20 µm and groove period of 20 µm. For this optimized design, an ultra-wide passband of approximately 400 GHz is found with a low signal reflection of below -8dB (approximately).

articleTitle: Hybrid Graphene and Gold Based Dynamically Tunable Triple Broadband Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This work presents a triple broadband metamaterial absorber using graphene and gold embedded in silica. We offer a transmission line-inspired method for achieving polarization-insensitive terahertz absorption over three wide frequency bands, enabling active control using gold and graphene. Our simulations show that graphene's Fermi energy (electrochemical potential) at 0.9 eV produces three absorption peaks of over 90% between 1.1 THz and 2.72 THz, 5.39 THz and 6.47 THz, and 9.25 THz and 10.97 THz for transverse electric (TE) waves (bandwidth 4.42 THz). For transverse magnetic (TM) waves, the bandwidth for which absorbance exceeds 90% is 4.29 THz between 1.14 THz and 2.64 THz, 5.51 THz and 5.5 THz, and 9.18 THz and 10.98 THz. Our metamaterial absorber maintains polarization (TE and TM) insensitivity and has significant absorption at incidence angles below 40°. Thus, a single layer of hybrid graphene-gold patch provides triple broadband absorption with a wide bandwidth and polarization insensitivity. Consequently, it holds promise for real-life applications such as electromagnetic wave absorption, tunable filtering, signal detection, modulators, and other broadband devices.

articleTitle: Computing Confinement Loss of Open-Channels Based PCF-SPR Sensor with ANN Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive spectroscopic technique for measuring changes in the refractive index (RI) of a medium in contact with a sensor surface. Confinement loss computation is crucial for designing an SPR-based photonic crystal fiber (PCF) sensor as it directly impacts its performance and sensitivity. The study highlights the simple and fast-training feed-forward Artificial Neural Network (ANN) as a technique for calculating the confinement loss of an open-channels-based PCF-SPR sensor. Moreover, ANN demonstrates proficiency in generating precise predictions for the aforementioned optical properties within the conventional parameter range, encompassing wavelengths between 0.60 μm and 0.90 μm, as well as an analyte RI range spanning from 1.33 to 1.40. Additionally, this work demonstrates a higher speed in predicting output values for varying sensor structural parameters than direct numerical simulation techniques. This study signifies a noteworthy progression in the field through the utilization of ANN-driven optimization methods for integrated silicon photonics devices. This advancement leads to improved speed and accuracy in nredicting sensor outputs.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-High Nonlinear Flint Glass Based Photonic Crystal Fiber with High Negative Dispersion over Telecom Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This study introduces an optimized ultra-high nonlinear photonic crystal fiber (UHN-PCF) design utilizing flint glass as the core material. The hexagonal cladding structure of the proposed photonic crystal fiber demonstrates remarkably high negative dispersion spanning the O to U wavelength range (1260 nm to 1675 nm), overcoming the inherent dispersive nature of flint glass. At the critical wavelength of 1550 nm, the fiber exhibits an exceptional negative dispersion value of −2241 ps/(nm•km), a crucial feature for high-speed data transmission systems. Additionally, the PCF structure showcases a remarkably high nonlinear coefficient of 720.8 (W•km)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at the same operating wavelength, suggesting potential applications in sensing and supercontinuum generation. The study employs the Finite Element Method to analyze various optical parameters, including effective area and confinement loss. These results underscore the fiber's suitability for long-distance communication systems and lay the groundwork for practical implementation in high-performance optical networks.

articleTitle: Numerical Performance Analysis of Soliton in Higher Nonlinear Medium Influenced by Quantum Potential
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: An optical soliton, also known as a soliton pulse, is a special kind of wavepacket that travels through a nonlinear medium with a constant speed, undistorted profile, and conserved energy and momentum. The nonlinear Schrödinger equation (NLSE) precisely balances the nonlinear and dispersion factors to produce this steady propagation. In this work, extensive numerical analysis is carried out to the NLSE with quadratic-cubic nonlinearity to describe the characteristics of optical soliton propagation. Specifically, we considered a perturbation term, quantum potential or the Bohm potential, to investigate the influence of perturbations on the propagation of optical solitons. The stability of the solitary pulse propagation by varying the strength of quantum potential, quadratic and cubic nonlinearities are well studied. To do so, we built a mathematical model of NLSE with quadratic-cubic nonlinearity and quantum potential and obtained the numerical solutions through the finite element method. We observed the stability and amplitude of the optical soliton pulse over a specific time interval for different values of the parameters. We investigated the suitable choice of parameters for stable pulse propagation. We found that optical soliton pulse propagation was stable when self-focusing nonlinearity equaled self-defocusing nonlinearity at a medium strength of quantum potential perturbation. In particular, for the Bohm potential, b= 0.4, and quadratic and cubic nonlinearity coefficients of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>= 0.3, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c$</tex> <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>=-0.3, stable soliton transmission was demonstrated which has less distortion and minimum amplitude variation. This model is important for studying the dynamics of solitons, perturbations in the transmission system, and optimizing the transmission system for stable soliton transmission.

articleTitle: Stabilisation of Cubic ZrO2 Thin Films Synthesized by Spray Pyrolysis: Influence of Cu Doping on Structural and Optical Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Nano-structured cubic Zirconium oxide (ZrO2) thin films have garnered considerable attention for its versatile use in gas sensors, fuel cells, nuclear reactors, and MOSFET gate dielectrics. In the present study, a facile Spray Pyrolysis technique was used to deposit pure and 2-8% Cu-doped Zr02 thin films annealed at 500° C for 1 hour and their structural and optical properties were investigated. All films exhibited single phase cubic polycrystalline structure that predominantly oriented along the (111) plane. The lattice constant of pure ZrO2 thin films is found to be 5.107 A which slightly decreases in Cu-doped films due to the incorporation of smaller Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ ions into larger Zr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>+ site. The crystallite sizes of the films were under 42 nm. All thin films exhibited ≥72 % transparency in the visible region with a maximum of 76.2% with 8% Cu doping. Pure ZrO2 thin films showed a bandgap of 3.96 eV which increased to 3.98 eV for 4 % Cu doping before returning to the initial value for the 8 % Cu-doped film. The unique characteristics of zirconia in its cubic stabilized form make it an ideal material for various photonic-enabled technologies.

articleTitle: Development of a Smart Antenna for Wireless Communication in ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Smart antenna technologies have introduced a new dimension to next-generation communication systems. This paper presents an innovative approach to smart antenna configuration for IoT applications in the 2.45 GHz ISM band. The proposed configuration, featuring a modified octagonal layout, enables dynamic beam direction adjustment according to user avail- ability and Direction of Arrival (DOA) with a new approach. The beam direction is regulated by using a low-cost Arduino Nano microcontroller connected to the nRF24L01 module. An algorithm is also presented to operate the proposed scheme. The real-time functionality of the proposed smart antenna system has been validated experimentally and presented in this paper. Smart antennas are crucial in the ISM band as they enhance signal quality, extend communication range and mitigate interference.

articleTitle: On Physical Layer Security Analysis of Hybrid RF/FSO Wireless Networks over k – μ/GG Channels with Pointing Error Impairments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The integration of mixed Radio Frequency (RF) and Free-Space Optical (FSO) wireless models in 6G wireless systems is pivotal for harnessing the complementary strengths of both technologies, enabling unprecedented levels of reliability, capacity, and security in next-generation networks. To address this combined use, this paper delves into the secrecy performance of a hybrid RF-FSO mixed model. Moreover, the transmitter and receiver establish communication through two distinct paths: the first link utilizes RF technology, characterized by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa-\mu$</tex> shadowed fading distribution, while the second link employs FSO technology, encountering Gamma-Gamma (GG) turbulence with pointing error impairment. At the receiver, a selection combining technique is employed to choose between the incoming signals. In order to analytically assess the improvement, we deduce the analytical expressions of secrecy outage probability (SOP) in closed form. Our findings substantiate that the hybrid RF- FSO model surpasses a single FSO/RF link in terms of secrecy outage probability. Finally, Monte Carlo simulations are conducted to validate the accuracy of the derived expressions.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Dual Channel PCF Based SPR Biosensor for Multi-Analyte Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this research, a highly sensitive multichannel Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF) based Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) sensor is presented for the detection of the refractive index (RI) of any unknown analyte. The proposed biosensor has two analyte slots, and it can detect two different analytes simultaneously. In Channel 1 (Ch-l), the employed plasmonic material is Gold (Au), whereas in Channel 2 (Ch-2), a combination of Gold and Tantalum Pentoxide (Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>) serves as the plasmonic material. The circular PCF incorporates a total of seventeen air holes which can be easily fabricated by applying existing fabrication techniques. Numerical analysis based on Finite element method (FEM) is used to simulate and assess the sensor's performance. The proposed sensor shows remarkable sensitivity in a broad sensing range of RI 1.33-1.41. The sensor attains maximum wavelength sensitivity of 11,000 nm/RIU for Ch-1 and 41,000 nm/RIU for Ch-2. Moreover, the sensor shows an impressive maximum amplitude sensitivity of 1459.34 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and 629.10 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> for channel-l and channel-2 respectively. To the best of our knowledge the proposed sensor achieves highest amplitude sensitivity compared to all other multi-channel sensors reported before. The minimum sensor resolution is 2.44 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–6</sup> refractive index unit (RIU). It is expected that our designed highly sensitive sensor will be effectively applied to identify a diverse range of substances, including chemicals, organic or inorganic compounds and other different analytes.

articleTitle: A Cooperative Mechanism to Speedup the Block Generation in Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In Blockchain, the Proof of Work (PoW) consensus algorithm is one of the most acceptable mechanisms for block generation and validation. However, the mining process of the PoW-based blockchain technology is slow because of its internal mechanism and competitive mining process. This paper proposes a new block-mining mechanism for blockchain-based cryptocurrencies. Unconfirmed transaction hashes reside in the memory pools (Mempool) of the blockchain network. In our proposed model, we utilize this Mempool in an efficient way for block generation. We introduce a new type of node called supervisor node to speed up this mining process. The traditional PoW-based approach creates a waste of the hash-solving power of the network miners. In our model, miners are controlled by those supervisor nodes. The supervisor nodes manage a shared mining process mechanism among those hired miners. Theoretical analysis of our proposed mechanism shows that this process can help remedy the hash-solving power wastage problem in Blockchain.

articleTitle: Enhanced Broadband Absorption in Crystalline Si Solar Cells with Parabola Textured Front Surface and Plasmonic Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Nanotextured front surface with sub-wavelength plasmonic properties shows excellent broad-spectrum light absorption capabilities in solar cells having extremely thin Si layers. In this study, we explore how periodic Si paraboloids, embedded with silver (Ag) nanoparticles (NPs), can effectively capture light and enhance the operational efficiency of solar cells. A layer of crystalline silicon (c-Si) with a thickness of 2 µm is used as the active medium and nano-paraboloids are utilized to channel incident solar rays into guided modes. To maximize absorption, we fine-tune the nanostructure geometry, periodicity, and Ag NP size. We observe an average absorption enhancement of 6.3% (in the wavelength span of 300 to 1600 nm) and 29% (in the span of 800 to 1600 nm) with nano-paraboloids coated with Ag NPs (diameter of 45 nm) compared to the uncoated nano-paraboloids.

articleTitle: Advancement in Breast Cancer Diagnosis: Detecting CA15-3 Antigen Using Surface Plasmon Resonance in Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This manuscript introduces a surface plasmon resonance sensor designed for the highly sensitive detection of the biomarker CA15-3, crucial for diagnosing Breast cancer. The sensor is based on an anisotropic dual-core, double-side-polished photonic crystal fiber. Analyzing analytes with refractive indices (RI) ranging from 1.33 to 1.36 RIU, the biosensor exhibits significant potential. The numerical analysis of sensing parameters reveals a peak wavelength sensitivity of 42,000 nm/RIU for x-polarization when employing the wavelength interrogation technique. The sensor demonstrates a maximum amplitude sensitivity of 105 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and achieves a remarkable sensor resolution of 3.6225 × 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>RIU.

articleTitle: A Slotted Monopole Patch Antenna Design for Ultra-Wideband Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-slot patch antenna that is designed, optimized, and analyzed for ultra-wideband (UWB) wireless applications. The designed antenna incorporates a compact dimension of 26x28x0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>and is structured on an FR-4 (lossy) substrate material with a partially slotted ground. It operates over a wider frequency ranging from 3.15 GHz to 10.79 GHz with a 10-dB impedance bandwidth ratio of 3.425:1. It has the lowest reflection coefficient of -47.5 dB at 3.5 GHz and also has two peaks of -43.13 dB and -29.93 dB at 5 GHz and 10 GHz respectively. It has a maximum gain of 3.22 dBi and a directivity of 3.95 dBi at 6.5 GHz. The overall efficiency of the designed UWB antenna is more than 80% and the maximum radiation efficiency of 93% is obtained at 3.35 GHz. The designed antenna exhibits the desired radiation characteristics essential for UWB wireless applications.

articleTitle: Photocatalytic-Degradation Induced Changes in Structural and Optical Properties of Gd-Doped TiO2 Ceramic Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this paper, the photocatalytic-degradation induced changes in the structural and optical properties of Gd-doped-Ti02 nanoparticles are investigated under Xenon-light emitting photocatalytic reactor. To identify the influence of doping on the change in properties after the photodegradation, we compare the performances of undoped and Gd-doped- TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> photocatalysts. The major structural and optical properties of both the undoped and doped TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are evaluated using standard material characterization tools before and after the photodegradation of Methylene Blue dye solution.

articleTitle: Secure Wireless Multicasting of RIS-Aided Wireless Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This research paper focuses on assessing the security performance of wireless communication networks assisted by reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) in scenarios involving multiple receivers and multiple eavesdroppers. Specially, an RIS is placed between the source and receivers to improve the link security. To illustrate the effect of various key parameters, such as the channels' average signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the number of reflecting elements within the RIS, and the number of eavesdroppers and receivers, we derive closed-form analytical expressions for the secure outage probability for multicasting (SOPM) and the probability of non-zero secrecy multicast capacity (PNSMC). Finally, we validate the accuracy of our analytical results through Monte-Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: A Highly Sensitive Simple Structured SPR Sensor for Refractive Index and Temperature Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: We propose a highly sensitive, simple microstructured photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor for refractive index (RI) and temperature detection using only eight circular air holes arranged in two rings. We use tantalum pentoxide (Ta<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>) along with gold (Au) as plasmonic material. The sensor exhibits highest wavelength sensitivity (WS) of 60000 nm/RIU, an amplitude sensitivity (AS) of 2117.31 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, a wavelength resolution (WR) of 1.67× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> RIU, an amplitude resolution (AR) of 4.72× 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> RIU, and a figure of merit (FOM) of 1500 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, with a detecting range from 1.29 to 1.42. Additionally, the sensor can also detect temperatures from 0°C to 160°C with a sensitivity (TS) of 24000 (pm/°C) for polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS).

articleTitle: Obfuscated Malware Detection: Investigating Real-World Scenarios Through Memory Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In the era of the internet and smart devices, the detection of malware has become crucial for system security. Malware authors increasingly employ obfuscation techniques to evade advanced security solutions, making it challenging to detect and eliminate threats. Obfuscated malware, adept at hiding itself, poses a significant risk to various platforms, including computers, mobile devices, and IoT devices. Conventional methods like heuristic-based or signature-based systems struggle against this type of malware, as it leaves no discernible traces on the system. In this research, we propose a simple and cost-effective obfuscated malware detection system through memory dump analysis, utilizing diverse machine-learning algorithms. The study focuses on the CIC-MaIMem-2022 dataset, designed to simulate real-world scenarios and assess memory-based obfuscated malware detection. We evaluate the effectiveness of machine learning algorithms, such as decision trees, ensemble methods, and neural networks, in detecting obfuscated malware within memory dumps. Our analysis spans multiple malware categories, providing insights into algorithmic strengths and limitations. By offering a comprehensive assessment of machine learning algorithms for obfuscated malware detection through memory analysis, this paper contributes to ongoing efforts to enhance cybersecurity and fortify digital ecosystems against evolving and sophisticated malware threats. The source code is made open-access for reproducibility and future research endeavours. It can be accessed at https://bit.ly/MaIMemCode

articleTitle: Bangla Handwriting Resource Generation and Recognition Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Maintaining cultural and linguistic diversity is a challenge in an increasingly digital world. For a language like Bangla, with a rich script and heritage, preserving the essence of handwritten text is crucial. The research employs a Deep Learning algorithm, to decipher the nuances of handwritten Bangla script. The algorithm learns to mimic the fluid strokes, unique characters, and artistic nuances intrinsic to handwritten Bangla text through extensive training on the authentic dataset. To democratize the use of this technology, a user-friendly model interface for generating handwritten Bangla text is developed. This model allows users, regardless of technical expertise, to seamlessly recognize digital text into beautiful handwritten Bangla imagery. However, preserving the essence of Bangla's handwritten beauty is not just an act of conservation; it's a testament to our commitment to cultural diversity. The paper addresses this challenge by proposing a novel approach to recognizing digital Bangla text into handwritten Bangla text in image format, leveraging an authentic Bangla dataset.

articleTitle: On the Performance of Intelligent Reflecting Surface Aided Industrial Internet of Things Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This paper considers an Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environment and explores the utilizations of Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) panels to improve the reliability of data transmissions. The effect of boundary walls and reflected signals in an indoor IIoT setting are accounted for in the analysis. Two multi-IRS-aided schemes are considered, that is, Exhaustive IRS-aided (ERA) scheme and Opportunistic IRS-aided (ORA) scheme, and their performances are evaluated by analyzing the outage probabilities (OPs). Extensive simulation studies under-score the significant improvements in wireless communication performance and reliability brought about by deploying IRS panels in IIoT environments.

articleTitle: A Compact E-Shape Patch Antenna for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: A small scaled rectangular patch antenna has been transformed into a novel E-shaped design, proving invaluable in wide-ranging 5G mm wave applications such as satellite communications, radar navigation, massive IoT, and WLAN networks. In this research, the suggested antenna provides a delightful triple band frequency coverage at 42.66 GHz, 61.32 GHz, and 76.32 GHz, each with a spectrum width of 2.04 GHz, 2.16 GHz, and a remarkable 14.28 GHz, respectively. Using CST simulation software, a compact 4 x 5 x 0.55 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> patch antenna is devised with a return loss <- 10 dB for each center frequency. It provides an overall antenna efficiency of 80% with a directivity above 7 dB.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of a Compact Implantable Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This work presents an implantable antenna for biomedical applications, which resonates at the ISM (industrial, scientific, and medical) band of 2.4–2.48 GHz when placed beneath the skin, precisely within the fat tissue among the three layers (skin, fat, and muscle) of the human-tissue phantom. The antenna is designed on a FR-4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\ {{\varepsilon }_{\bm{r}}} = {\mathrm{ }}4.3{\mathrm{ }}and{\mathrm{ }}tan\delta = 0.025)$</tex> substrate of 0.36 mm thickness. The design is based on a defected ground structure (DGS) and a shorting pin between patch and ground, both of which helps to reduce the antenna size by lengthening its electrical path. Furthermore, the antenna is encapsulated with biocompatible silicon <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\ {{\varepsilon }_r} = 11.9{\mathrm{ }}and{\mathrm{ }}\sigma = 0.00025{\mathrm{ }}S/m)$</tex> superstrates of 0.5 mm thickness. The proposed antenna is very compact in dimension <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$( {8\ \times \ 6\ \times \ 1.36} )$</tex> mm³, while provides high bandwidth and gain of 10.57% and -20.10 dBi, respectively. The antenna is simulated using CST to investigate its performance. At the center frequency of 2.46 GHz, input impedance of the antenna is found to be (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50.09\ + \ 1.17)\ \Omega$</tex>, which assists a good impedance matching, resulting a VSWR of 1.02. Finally, the link margin is calculated to establish far-field communication, which shows that the antenna supports a high data rate of 1 Mbps up to a distance of about 9 m for SAR limited power.

articleTitle: Photocatalytic and Optical Modulation of δ-MnO2 Nanoflowers with Surface Morphology and Disorder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this work, the δ polymorph of MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nano-flowers (NFs) with two different surface morphologies were hydrothermally synthesized by changing the cooling technique. The slow oven-cooled NFs exhibited superior photocatalytic efficiency than the fast air-cooled ones. The structural and optical study revealed a reduction in effective optical band gap with an enhanced growth of nano-petal-like structures on MnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> particle surfaces for the slow cooling process. The augmentation observed in photo-degradation kinetics was explicated in terms of a change in surface texturing associated with nano-petal growth and defect-induced destabilization of excitons.

articleTitle: Structural-dependent Performance of Au Nano-Wire Blended D-Shaped SPR Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) is one of the promising techniques in the field of refractive index sensing, which assists in achieving ultra-high sensitivity, real-time, label-free detection with versatile chemical and biochemical sensing capabilities. The SPR phenomenon is the oscillation of electrons in a metal-dielectric interface with incident light. This study thoroughly evaluates the performance of a D-shaped single-mode optical fiber-based SPR sensor with different shapes of gold nano-wire to enhance the detection sensitivity. Four different nano-wires-based sensors including circular-shaped, square-shaped, triangular-shaped, and rectangular-shaped are investigated. The maximum wavelength sensitivities found are 50,000 nm/RIU, 40,000 nm/RIU, 40,000 nm/RIU, and 60,000 nm/RIU for circular, square, triangular, and rectangular nano-wires-based SPR sensors, respectively. In addition, comprehensive investigations show that the maximum amplitude sensitivities for circular, square, triangular, and rectangular nano-wire are 71.871 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 23.615 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 23.661 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and 59.558 RIU<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, respectively. The RI range of 1.40 to 1.405 covers the polyacrylonitrile liquid which combines the binary mixtures of acrylonitrile with ethanol, methanol, propan-1-ol, etc., where we discovered the highest sensitivity.

articleTitle: Low Loss and Birefringent Hollow-core Anti-Resonant Fiber for THz Waveguiding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: A nested anti-resonant hollow core fiber has been proposed for low transmission loss with birefringence for THz application. In this work, two horizontal circular tubes and four vertical nested tubes have been used with TOPAS as fiber material. The symmetry of the fiber structure has been broken by introducing different horizontal tube diameter. Therefore, the symmetry is broken in the cladding of the fiber. The proposed fiber has got the highest birefringence 1.12 x 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>, an optimum confinement loss of 0.062 dB/m and 0.10 dB/m for X-polarized and Y-polarized light respectively. The effective material loss (EML) is 0.03 dB/m and 0.02 dB/m for X-polarized and Y-polarized light respectively. The proposed fiber could have been a good choice for the application of polarizing filter, biomedical imaging, optical communication etc.

articleTitle: Carcinogenic Element Detection in Water Using Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) Based Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an investigation conducted to examine the utilization of a Photonic Crystal Fiber (PCF) sensor incorporating Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) technology to identify carcinogenic substances present in water samples, such as Nickel, Arsenic, 1-4 Dioxane, Chloroform, and Asbestos. The proposed configuration of our sensor entails applying a chemically stable gold material as an internal coating on a circular PCF, preceded by the deposition of a thin layer of gold (Au) onto the fiber. To evaluate key performance parameters such as sensitivity, wavelength sensitivity, amplitude sensitivity, and resolution, we employed the COMSOL Multiphysics software in conducting simulations. We numerically evaluated the suggested sensor using the finite element method. The findings show that the gold-coated analyte layer in a round PCF surface is a reliable sensor for carcinogenic substances present in water. With a remarkable wavelength sensitivity of 6136.364 nmRIU-1 for 1,4-dioxane, an amplitude sensitivity of -500.572 RIU-1 for arsenic, and a maximum resolution of 1.64 × 10-5 RIU for Chloroform within the detection range (1.3300-1.5563).

articleTitle: SatNet: A Lightweight Satellite Image Classification Model Using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Deep Learning approach is essential for classifying remotely sensed images, identifying objects in satellite images, and using those results for numerous purposes. In light of the large number of datasets, image classification requires high accuracy and training performance, making the approach crucial to developing reliable and accurate classification models. As the field of satellite imaging has advanced, researchers are more inclined to rely on techniques for the automatic and efficient classification of satellite images. However, many well-known networks need a lot of parameters and computing power, which makes them challenging to use for classification tasks. A Lightweight Deep Convolutional Neural Network (Deep CNN) called SatNet is proposed for satellite image categorization which uses less computing power and is an efficient model for multiclass classification problems. Five transfer learning models - Xception, InceptionV3, VGG19, ResNet50, and DenseNet201 were taken into consideration in order to make comparisons. The Satellite Image Classification Dataset-Rsi-cb256is used by the model during testing. It effectively outperforms other measures and surpasses ResNet50 and VGG19 outputs, with an accuracy rate of 99.15%. A quicker and easier method of classifying satellite image data is possible with the proposed Deep CNN model.

articleTitle: Refractometric Sensing of Waterborne Pathogens by Photonic Crystal Fiber Sensor in THz Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: An accurate detection approach is essential for identifying waterborne pathogens due to the high threat to human health. Considering the harmfulness of waterborne pathogens, a photonic crystal fiber sensor has been proposed and numerically evaluated the optical properties in the THz regime. Finite element method-based Comsol Multiphysics software has been utilized to design and analyze the PCF sensor. The proposed sensor renders superior performances for all the tested cases including a high sensitivity of 99.142% for vibrio cholera 99.324% for E. coli 99.35% for enterococcus faecalis and very low confinement loss of 1.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> dB/cm for vibrio cholera, 1.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> dB/cm for E. coli and 1.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> dB/cm for enterococcus faecalis at 4.8 THz operating frequency. Fabrication potential in the existing fabrication platform and a possible experimental setup for testing the sensor are also discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Highly Efficient SnSe Solar Cell with CuI as an HTL by SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In the present article, a semiconducting tin selenide (SnSe) absorber-based novel heterostructure device of FTO/CdS/SnSe/CuI/Ni is modeled by exploiting SCAPS-1D program. Herein, the copper iodide (CuI) as a hole transport layer (HTL) is employed at the rear of SnSe active material and rear metal electrode. The SCAPS-1D program is also exploited to evaluate the photovoltaic (PV) output parameters of the suggested new solar device. It is discovered that that p+ type CuI as an HTL confirms modest band structure at the SnSe/CuI junction, thus minimizing the carrier recombination at rear contact. As a result, the open circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>) is increased up to 0.86 V for the cell with an HTL. Also, the efficiency is increased from 17.58% to 24.57% after adding the CuI HTL in the anticipated SnSe-based PV device. Furthermore, the PV performances of the designed device employing an HTL have been analyzed by the thickness, carrier density, defect level, and operating temperature. These outputs intimate that the CuI can be introduced as a promising HTL material for the developing inexpensive and high-efficiency SnSe-based PV devices.

articleTitle: A Branch-Line Coupler Feed MIMO Antenna for Circular Polarization Diversity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: A 2-element microstrip multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with circular polarization (CP) diversity is reported for 5G wireless applications in the sub-6 GHz band. The MIMO configuration in a single layer consisting of two square-shaped radiating elements, each with two input ports, is implemented on a shared ground surface. The attainment of CP diversity is facilitated by incorporating a 90º branch-line coupler (BLC) inside the feed network. The generation of a ±90º out-of-phase signal, which is utilized to excite left-hand CP (LHCP) and right-hand CP (RHCP) signals by means of orthogonal feed lines of each patch, is achieved by employing a 90º BLC. Additionally, enhanced isolation can be attained by implementing a T-shaped slot on the shared ground plane using a defective-ground approach positioned between two antenna elements. For LHCP/RHCP, a measured 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 4.81% is obtained. Moreover, a satisfactory CP radiation performance is attained in the operating frequency of 3.45–3.62 GHz. In addition, the measured envelope correlation coefficient exhibits a value below 0.01, indicating enhanced performance in MIMO applications.

articleTitle: Consistency of Peak Wavelength with Higher Absorption of GaN Nanowire Arrays : Independency on Filling Fraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Nanowire (NW) arrays offer improved optical confinement compared to single nanowires, but their performance heavily depends on the filling fraction value. This study aims to explore the relationship between different filling fractions and various radii of GaN nanowires integrated with Silicon substrates and an Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) top contact using finite difference time domain (FDTD) analysis. These findings indicate that nanowires with radii of 50 nm and 60 nm exhibit consistent behavior with respect to filling fraction, forming a distinct cluster in terms of maximum absorbance and peak wavelengths. In contrast, nanowires with different radii display more scattered behavior. Interestingly, 55 nm radius-based nanowires show an independent peak at approximately 375 nm, regardless of the filling fraction. Nanowires with radii of both 50 nm and 60 nm exhibit similar behavior, sharing a consistent peak wavelength of 378 nm, and this consistency remains unaffected by variations in the filling fraction. These insights shed light on fabrication flexibility in optimizing nanowire-based devices for improved performance and integration in optoelectronic applications.

articleTitle: Low Power Higher Order Gaussian Pulse Generator using Triangular Inverting Pulse Shaper
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This work demonstrates a fully integrated on-off-keying (OOK) Gaussian pulse generator (PG) using a triangular inverting pulse shaper (TIPS), resulting in improved output swing and higher efficiency without needing an additional buffer stage. The TIPS, combined with a high pass filter, ensures a high peak-to-peak voltage and conforms with the power spectral density (PSD) of the FCC (Federal Communications Commission) indoor spectral mask. This Gaussian PG operates at a low power of approximately 0.87 mW for a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of 100 MHz and can generate pulse orders starting from the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and higher. Based on 90-nm CMOS technology, the simulation results demonstrate peak to peak voltage swing and pulse width variations ranging from 571- 654 mV and 390–632 ps, respectively, where the supply voltage is 1.2 V. Additionally, the TIPS is able to maintain the Gaussian shape for higher-order pulses, which is difficult to achieve using an ordinary filter set-up.

articleTitle: Design of Rectennas at 7.30 GHz for RF Power Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Wireless power transfer is gaining interest in harvesting energy from radio frequency (RF) signals by rectennas. This paper proposes two rectenna systems for RF power harvesting at 7.30 GHz employing a half-wave rectifier and a three-stage Dickson rectifier. The development is carried out using the equivalent circuit of an antenna with Advance Design Software (ADS) and the proposed rectenna system is simulated with LTspice. Firstly, ADS is used to develop and optimize the dual-band antenna's equivalent RLC circuit at 7.30 GHz and 9.50 GHz. Next, the two rectifier topologies in the rectenna system are developed, and their performance is evaluated in terms of output power, load resistance, input and output voltage. It is found that the rectenna system using a three-stage Dickson rectifier provides 2.28 times higher output voltage than a half-wave rectifier while the input voltage is 250 mV and the load is 6.5 KΩ. Results also show that the output power level for the three-stage Dickson rectifier is -20 dBm to 9.24 dBm whereas the output power level for half wave is -20 dBm to 31.7 dBm.

articleTitle: RESCUED: Robust Quantum Error Correction with Surface Code in Noisy Channels Using Ensemble Decoder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The necessity for quantum error correction arises from the need to safeguard quantum information from errors induced by decoherence and other noise forms. However, the optimal decoding of quantum error-correcting codes is a computationally challenging task. In our research, we introduce an ensemble decoder that amalgamates the advantages of various decoders to attain lower logical error rates and the capability to decode multiple errors. We employed statistical methodologies to allocate a specific error syndrome to the decoder with the highest likelihood of accurate decoding. We applied diverse variants of the Noise model to simulate the impact of noise on transmitted quantum states accurately. The efficacy of the ensemble decoder was assessed in both Symmetric and Asymmetric Noise Models. In the Symmetric Noise Model, bit-flip and phase-flip errors are presumed to have equal probabilities, while in the Asymmetric Noise Model, these probabilities can vary. The comparison aimed to evaluate the ensemble decoder's proficiency in rectifying these error types compared to traditional decoding techniques. Our results indicate that the ensemble decoder surpasses conventional decoders in the Symmetric Noise model, particularly for higher code distances. It is also apparent that augmenting the lattice size diminishes the logical error rate and that threshold and pseudo-threshold values escalate with incremental changes in noise asymmetry. The study's findings underscore the substantial potential of the ensemble decoder in quantum error correction and communication realms.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Low Power Low Noise Graphene Mosfet based VCO for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This paper presents a 3-stage ring voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) designed in 90 nm Graphene CMOS technology where gate capacitance of the MOSFET is used to regulate the oscillation frequency. Through deep analysis and performance evaluation, Leeson's model is used in MATLAB (R2022b) Simulink software to find oscillation frequency, operating frequency range, phase noise and power consumption. The analytical approach shows, Graphene MOSFET capacitance based ring VCO offers a linear tuning characteristic ranging from 21.5 GHz to 24.25 GHz, which is much higher than traditional ring VCO for a range of small control voltage. The variation of control voltage differs from 0 V to 0.2 V with a supply voltage of 1.8 V. Simulated figure of merit (FoM) is -166.88 dBc/Hz and the voltage sensitivity is 125 MHz/V. Low phase noise, low power consumption and ultra-high frequency of oscillation make the proposed design an excellent candidate for future high-speed wireless electronic circuit and 5G applications.

articleTitle: Design of Photonic Crystal Ring Resonator Based AND Gate and Transmission Gate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this work, we have presented the design of an optical AND gate and a Transmission gate based on photonic crystal ring resonator. The structure is composed of circular silicon rods in air. The band diagram has been generated using the equations of wave vector in Brillouin Zone and corresponding bandgap and associated wavelength range have been calculated. Both the gate structure is combination of two ring resonators formed on 13.2μm by 8.4μm substrate. The input combinations are simulated and the corresponding outputs are verified with truth table of the gates. The performance in terms of contrast ratio has been found to be 16.2dB for both the gates.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis for Bengali Handwritten Character & Digit Recognition Using Capsule Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: At the present time handwritten character recognition is the most demandable and interesting topic to work on for many research areas and projects. A lot of work has already been done on Bengali handwritten character recognition. We proposed Bengali handwritten character recognition (HCR) using Capsule Network. It is a deep-learning technique and has never been used in this area except for Bengali handwritten digit recognition. We have tried different Bengali character datasets, among them Bornomala Dataset(Bornomala Fifty) was more reliable as the data was cleaned and processed already. The regularly used machine-learning techniques really struggle with rotated images. Capsule Network works very amazingly in the case of rotated images. We have tested our model with images that are rotated 50 degrees to both the left and right side. We provide a comparative study of recognizing Bangla handwritten character and digit using capsule network. The predicted accuracy is achieved 81.29% for characters, 95.57% for digits and 81% for number and digit combination.

articleTitle: A Polarization Insensitive Achromatic Metalens Operating at Two Wavelengths in Visible Regime
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Metasurface, the 2D equivalent of metamaterial, is becoming popular in lens designing for its dimension in the order of wavelength of light. Usage of a single lens with light sources of different wavelengths has been a challenge as the focal length tends to deviate. Here, we show the design procedure of a TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(a low loss dielectric) based polarization insensitive metalens utilizing the idea of an interleaved structure that is able to maintain less than 1% focal length deviation between two different wavelengths (600 nm and 650 nm) in the visible spectrum. We also show for comparison purposes that a conventional metalens designed at a single wavelength (600 nm) shows a deviation of 8.66% in focal length between the two wavelengths. Lastly, we demonstrate the polarization-insensitive behavior of our designed metalens. So, our metalens can be a promising tool for imaging, spectroscopy, etc. in the visible regime where bi-wavelength operation is necessary.

articleTitle: Development of an Automated Air Quality Monitoring System for Data Centers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: A modern data center is equipped with servers, computers, and network equipment running 24 hours to meet the huge computational demands of the host organization. It is critical to keep an eye on the air quality parameters so that essential actions can be made in the event of an emergency. Small to Medium Enterprises (SME) and academic sectors, particularly in poor nations, are unable to purchase readily available, and expensive modern monitoring and regulating equipment. This paper presents the development of a low-cost microcontroller-based air quality monitoring system for a data center. It consists of a micro-controller, gas sensors, and a humidity and temperature sensor for detecting Carbon Dioxide, Carbon Mono-oxide, Liquefied Petroleum Gas leakage, humidity, temperature, and the display devices. The results have been compared with that of a standard data center which validates the accuracy and performance of the system. The cost of the system is also estimated which shows that it is much lower than the same types of products that are available in the market.

articleTitle: (1-x)BaTiO3 - xLi0.1Ni0.2Mn0.6Fe2.1O4 Based Multiferroics: Structure and Dielectric Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The conventional solid-state reaction route was used to synthesize a multiferroic system with composition: (1-x)BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>[BTO] - xLi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</inf>Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.1</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>[LNMFO]. The samples were sintered within a temperature range of 1000 - 1400°C to optimize the process temperature. From X-ray diffraction analysis, the BTO and LNMFO phases exhibited tetragonal per-ovskite and cubic spinal structures, respectively. A conspicuous variation in microstructural morphology with system composition was observed from micrographic analysis. The sample dielectric responses were measured utilizing the a.c. impedance spectro-scopic technique. Although a large dielectric spectral dispersion was observed in the case of pure BTO(x=0), the composite (x=0.5) exhibited an impressive dielectric stability region with high permittivity and a very low dielectric loss. The findings could help improve the performance of magneto-dielectric composite-based systems

articleTitle: Highly Coherent Supercontinuum Generation in a Silicon Nanowire with Sub-Wavelength Air-Hole
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this paper, we describe possible supercontinuum generation (SCG) in a special silicon nanowire with a central air hole. The addition of an air hole enhances the nonlinearity of nanowire structures which already exhibit highly nonlinear properties. This results in an wideband and coherent SCG spectrum. We demonstrate the dependency of the optical mode characteristics and the bandwidth of the spectrum on the air hole size and are able to estimate a maximum bandwidth of 370 THz for a low pulse power of 300 W at 2 μm wavelength, which is significantly higher than that obtained without the air hole.

articleTitle: An Exploration of Lead-Free Sb2Se3 Thin Film Solar Cell with Graphene as Hole Transport Layer Using SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Thin-film solar cells (TFSCs) have captured an enormous attention in recent times owing to their adaptability, afford-ability, and compact size. Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> has promising characteristics as a viable absorber material for TFSCs by virtue of its remarkable absorption coefficient, tunable bandgap, and cost-effectiveness. Yet, Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based TFSCs have been hampered in their commercialization by the conventional HTLs limited stability and degradation issues. The unique optical and electrical properties of graphene can make it an ideal HTL for Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based TFSCs. This study represents the optimization of Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-based TFSC with the following structure: ITO/WS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Graphene/Au, where Graphene has been inserted as an HTL layer to accomplish proper band alignment and diminish recombination loss at the rear electrode. This study also examines the influence of interface defects, shunt and series resistance, temperature, J-V characteristics, and quantum efficiency (QE) on the performance parameters of solar cell. The SCAPS-1D simulator has been used to attain an efficiency of 26.74% with a V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf> value of 0.8475 V, Jsc value of 37.46 mA/cm2, and FF value of 84.20%. The observations of this study offer an effective approach for producing cost-effective and high-performing Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> solar cells by using the suitable HTL.

articleTitle: Tuning of the Structural, Optical and Magnetic Properties of BiFeO3 Nanoparticles by Annealing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: High purity BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles were synthesized via solgel process in this work. The effect of the annealing temperature on structural, optical and magnetic properties were studied. The X-ray diffraction analysis showed a distorted perovskite structure where phase purity could be tuned by varying annealing temperature. At higher temperatures, the particle size increased and the band gap decreased. Analysis of magnetic property revealed the presence of weak ferromagnetism in the BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles. The study indicates that the functional properties of the nanoparticles could be tuned to accommodate both photovoltaic and photocatalytic applications.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-LSTM Transfer Learning for Dengue Diagnosis from Raman Spectroscopy Images
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The diagnosis of dengue fever can be made quickly and effectively with Raman spectroscopy. However, the diagnostic procedure presents difficulties; for example, the distinction between healthy and infected spectra is extremely subtle. Deep learning (DL)-based diagnosis of dengue from Raman spectroscopy is gaining research interest. This paper introduces an innovative hybrid model that combines the architecture of a long-short-term memory recurrent neural network (LSTM RNN) with the capabilities of a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN). We present the CNN-LSTM Transfer Learning (HCL-TL) method, which uses Raman spectroscopy images to transform the field of data-driven dengue disease diagnosis. The proposed approach utilizes hyperparameters to refine the DL models. Both the initial training and subsequent fine-tuning stages incorporate model checkpoints and callbacks to monitor loss and prevent overfitting. A dataset consisting of 635 spectra-460 of which were infected and 175 of which were healthy-was used to evaluate the suggested model. Both holdout and 10-fold cross-validation methods are used for splitting the data samples. When applied to testing data for dengue infection diagnosis, the proposed HCL- TL method achieves a classification accuracy of 97.73%. The HCL-TL method outperforms the state-of-the-art DL and machine learning models in terms of accurately classifying dengue fever from Raman spectroscopy images, according to the results.

articleTitle: Innovative Evolutionary Algorithm for the Design and Optimization of Meta-material Absorbers in the Solar Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Efficiently capturing photons from the solar spec-trum is crucial for effective solar energy harvesting. To enhance photon absorption, there has been a growing interest in meta-material absorbers in recent years. Yet, designing and selecting parameters for these absorbers remains challenging due to their complex multi-physics properties. In this article, a new technique for designing meta-material absorber is studied using an interlink of simulation and optimization algorithm.
