Comsol Multiphysics software is used to simulate a metal-insulator-metal structure (Ni-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Ni in this case) to calculate average absorbance in solar spectrum of 200 - 2000 nm. A new innovative evolutionary algorithm is proposed to use this average absorbance as objective function for optimizing design parameters of the metamaterials more efficiently and reliably. A database is introduced in the algorithm to minimize the execution time. The proposed algorithm requires negligible simulation time compared to the traditional trial and error method and has improved initial average absorbance from 89.1% to 93.36%. Further analysis reveals that, on average, there is an absorbance of 92.37% in the ultraviolet range, 98.03% in the visible band, and 94.29% in the near-infrared range, with a peak absorption of 99.99% occurring at a wavelength of 650 nm. In addition, the proposed broad-band solar absorber presented in this work, can be used in optimizing the design of meta-materials for other applications with multiple objectives.

articleTitle: Developing an Integrated Platform for Different Network Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Integration of complex networks are essential for communication systems in the rapidly evolving technological landscape in today's world. However, managing and operating a large and diverse network with devices from multiple vendors can be a challenging task. Vendors may use different technologies, protocols, and interfaces which are bringing difficulties for network administrators to manage the network. The objective of this research is to develop an integrated platform for different network devices from different vendors. This integrated environment will be implemented by executing a designed script to configure the settings to operate different network devices. This proposed platform will mitigate the challenges of using different network devices in a complex platform. This study provides an integrated environment where it is easy to manage different technologies, protocols and interfaces. It also reduces time consumption for system configuration significantly comparing to manual configuration. The average time per device is 0.175 seconds whereas in previous studies the time was 3.33 seconds.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Model to Investigate Supercontinuum Generation in Chalcogenide Planar Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This study introduces a Deep Learning (DL) approach to predict supercontinuum generation in optical waveguides, addressing computational and time challenges of traditional numerical methods. The novel Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model, trained from scratch, demonstrates impressive accuracy in forecasting supercontinuum spectral bandwidth with a mean squared error of 0.017. Notably, the ANN model dramatically accelerates computations, taking only half the time of simulations in COMSOL Multiphysics and MATLAB. This DL-powered model presents a promising alternative for predicting supercontinuum generation, effectively overcoming resource constraints and complexity associated with conventional numerical methods.

articleTitle: SHAP Analysis: Identification of Factors Enhancing Diabetes Detection Using Boosting Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic disease caused by the presence of elevated blood sugar levels. Significant reductions in the risk factor and severity of diabetes can be achieved by the attainment of accurate early prediction capabilities. Due to limited data availability and the highly confidential nature of data, diabetes prediction imposes a significant challenge to the researchers. Again the presence of outliers or missing values within diabetes datasets makes the algorithms perform poorly in diabetes prediction. Moreover, various types of features are available in the datasets. There are some crucial features that affect the results of diabetic prediction. This study focused on the identification of shapely additive explanations(SHAP) values to find the most important features in diabetes prediction using the Boosting algorithms. The study also exploits three different datasets originating from Bangladesh, India, and Germany undergo a thorough investigation using SHAP analysis.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Metamaterial Absorber for the Solar Spectrum in the Visible Regime
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: An ultrathin metamaterial absorber is suggested in this work for visible solar radiation entrapment, using 3 layers of materials (Tungsten-Rexolite-Tungsten). A near-unity wideband absorbance is observed within all the visible wavelengths (380-750 nm). The Finite Integration technique is implemented for analyzing the absorber. The mean absorption is 97.01% in the respective visible regime. The resonant wavelength is 497.9 nm corresponding to a peak absorption of 99.96%. The performance of the structure is analyzed for different oblique incident angles as well as mechanical loading for implementation in a realistic solar energy harvesting scenario. The findings of the study indicate a wide-angle stability of the structure (up to 70°) and mechanical flexibility without facing a substantial decrease in absorbance.

articleTitle: An Optimized Dual Core Micro-structured Fiber for Splitting Applications at Communication Wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Numerical method is utilized to obtain different important optical properties of a dual core photonic crystal fiber which are vital and essential for effective and dependable optical communications. By changing important structural parameters, a simple design of DC-PCF has been optimized for efficient polarization and wavelength splitting. The proposed design has the potential to be used as a polarization splitter with a small device length and extremely low loss which is capable of decoupling two orthogonal polarized modes with a length of 2.33 mm at a wavelength of 1550 nm. Furthermore, it can be used as a demultiplexer where at an ultra-short device length of 0.334 mm, x-polarized modes of 1550 nm and 1000 nm can be separated and at length of 0.341 mm, y-polarized modes at same wavelengths can also be separated. This short-length polarization and wavelength splitter with low loss is well-suited for applications in integrated optical communications systems.

articleTitle: A Design of Antenna for UWB Application with Double Band-Notch Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This paper presents a new design of an antenna for UWB application covering the frequency range 3.1 - 10.6 GHz. Band-notched characteristics have also been incorporated in order to avoid interference with WLAN and X-band satellite downlink communications. Electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure has been employed to reject the signals from the WLAN frequency range, and split ring resonator (SRR) has been used to reject 7.5 GHz centered frequency. This (41 x 47 x 1.52mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) sized reference structure is designed on TLY-5A substrate with dielectric constant (fer) of 2.17 and tangent loss of 0.0009.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Chemically Functionalized Two-Dimensional Bilayer Hexagonal Gallium Nitride from First Principles Calculations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Optical Properties of Functionalized Graphene-like Gallium Nitride have been studied using First Principles. A comparison between the monolayer and bilayer structures indicates that bilayers possess a reduced bandgap than monolayers. In addition, the investigation reveals bilayer structures possess enhanced optical properties in comparison to monolayers, which can be utilized in optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: mTOVA: A Multilingual Task Oriented Virtual Assistant for Human Computer Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: A task-oriented virtual assistant (VA) refers to an ar-tificial intelligence-driven system that can assist users to perform daily activities. The utilisation of deep learning algorithms has enabled VAs to attain noteworthy advancements in high-resource languages, such as English. However, languages with limited resources, such as Bengali, have not encountered significant advancements in this domain. In this paper, we propose a multilingual task oriented voice-to-voice conversational agent, which is capable of proficiently managing diverse tasks such as weather forecast, date & time query, hospital and blood bank search etc in both Bengali and English language. Our developed system can understand voice command using Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Natural Language Understanding Unit (NL U). Then the system generates an appropriate reply by gathering information from the internet via APIs, data retrieval techniques and by employing dialogue management. Finally, Natural Language Generator (NLG) and Text to Speech (TTS) techniques are used to construct and deliver proper response. We integrated all the units using RASA framework and python script. Our developed ASR system has an average word error rate of 13% and NLU system has an intent and entity extraction accuracy of 93 % and 96.2 % respectively. The overall action prediction accuracy of our developed system is 99.4 %.

articleTitle: Discrete Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution: Security and Noise Tolerance Enhanced by Decoy States and Effective Error Correction Protocol Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: As the possibility of a genuine, functioning quantum computer becomes closer to reality every day, so does the urge to use the principles of quantum physics to improve the security of communications. One of the most studied areas of quantum communication is quantum key distribution (QKD), however there are still challenges to overcome, such as low detection accuracy, the need for extensive computation, and the lack of extremely efficient error correction. Even though Continuous Variable QKD has seen some significant advancements, there hasn't been much effort to integrate these advancements to make the CVQKD system stronger. By combining discrete modulation, the use of decoy states with the combination of cascade reconciliation and effective polar code-based error correction, our work aims to make the CVQKD more feasible for practical implementation and offer a secure, accurate, and noise-resistant Q KD protocol.

articleTitle: Design of a Split Ring Resonator Integrated Triple-Band Ridge SIW Bandpass Filter on Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This research aims to develop a triple-band bandpass filter using ridge substrate integrated waveguide (RSIW) technology with high transmission and rejection capabilities. The filter is realized by two metallic planes separated by a substrate, and rows of metallic vias are placed to connect the edges of the two metallic layers. A rectangular-shaped metallic ridge is inserted in the substrate horizontally. These multilayer structures are designed and analyzed in search of sharp multiband characteristics. To enhance the filter performance, split-ring resonators, and defected ground structure are introduced on the top and ground planes. The size of the proposed bandpass filter is 1.52λg × 1.52λg. The three passbands are from 10.51 GHz to 12.74 GHz with a bandwidth of 2.23 GHz, from 14.68 GHz to 15.96 GHz with a bandwidth of 1.28 GHz, and from 17.09 GHz to 18.88 GHz with a bandwidth of 1.79 GHz. Minimum insertion loss values for the three bands are 0.19 dB, 0.68 dB, and 0.63 dB, respectively, with return loss values below 11 dB. The proposed bandpass filter can play a significant role in X- and Ku-band wireless communication-based applications.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Multi-Amplitude Multi-Frequency Digital Modulation and Demodulation Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The basic binary modulation techniques, namely, ASK, FSK and PSK are seldom used in standard digital communications as they offer low bitrates. To achieve higher bitrates, sophisticated strategies like M-PSK and M-QAM are used, and M-FSK is not favored as this requires higher bandwidth than the other multi-level schemes. The performance analysis of the proposed Multi-Amplitude Multi-Frequency (MA-MF) modulation scheme has been conducted to investigate its suitability in possible bit-rate compression of digital signals. Here, parallel single-bin FFT algorithms are used instead of the traditional detection schemes, and multiple modulation frequencies are chosen to be the exact harmonic frequencies of the FFT. The proposed scheme appears to offer improved BER performance over the former. It has also been identified that if all possible frequencies of the FFT window are chosen for modulation, the proposed scheme leads to a scheme like OFDM, which is commonly used for multiplexing multiple digital channels. The differences and similarities between the proposed MA-MF and OFDM schemes are also presented.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of a c-Si Thin-Film Solar Cell Using Plasmonic Ag Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This article presents a study on the use of surface plasmon enhancement in n-p junction crystalline silicon-based thin-film solar cells. A back reflector using periodically ordered Ag nanostructures, along with a planar front layer that contains an inverted triangle groove pattern are used to design the cell structure. The main purpose of the front layer is to enhance the absorption of shorter wavelengths of incident light. To demonstrate higher absorption at longer wavelengths, a back reflector using nanostructure components, and an inverted triangular groove architecture are included. The average absorption area of our structure is around 84.36% within the spectral range of 300-1100nm. Our proposed structure has achieved a maximum current density, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf> of 40.66 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and an efficiency of 17.25%. Moreover, we have conducted an investigation into the impact of the length of the unit cell's period on the efficiency of our proposed cell. The results of our study demonstrate that the period length of the proposed unit cell exhibits better performance in comparison to others. Furthermore, a comprehensive examination of the electrical properties of thin-film solar cells has been carried out at various angles of light incidence ranging from 0 to 60 degrees whereas our proposed structure reveals a remarkable performance.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Graphene-Based Hyperbolic Metamaterials for Enhanced Light Absorption in Planar Si Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: This article discusses the graphene-based hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) used as the anti-reflection (AR) coating of planar Si solar cells. It theoretically and graphically represents the properties (conductivity, permittivity) of the proposed structure. A comprehensive analysis is conducted through meticulous research, exploring its performance across multiple modes, such as refractive, reflective, and absorbing modes. Notably, this investigation has placed particular emphasis on the absorbing mode of graphene, enabling us to accurately determine the absorbing power capacity. This significant finding opens up promising opportunities for the application of graphene in solar cells, thereby improving absorptance, generation rate, and short-circuit current density in the visible solar spectrum. The generation rate of planar Si solar cells is increased from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.1033 \times {10}^{27}{m}^{ - 3}{s}^{ - 1}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.28093 \times {10}^{27}{m}^{ - 3}{s}^{ - 1}$</tex> by using HMM in place of hBN. The current density is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$27.3\ mAc{m}^{ - 2}$</tex> for using HMM as AR of planar Si solar cell, marking a remarkable 106% enhancement compared to the Planar structure and 3.8% compared to the hBN based solar cell.

articleTitle: Au Decorated MoS2 for Selective Detection of Acetone at Room Temperature - Modeling, Simulation, and Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Sensitive gas sensors are becoming important for protecting human health and environmental monitoring. Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) has been considered a potential material for high sensitivity and selectivity acetone gas detection at ambient temperature due to its high certain area of surface and numeral active sites. Taking into account the limited research on the theoretical simulation of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas sensors, this work is focused on the modeling and simulation of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-based acetone gas sensors using COMSOL Multiphysics. The incorporation of gold nanoparticles on MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> causes further enhancement of sensitivity toward acetone. The MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-Au sensor showed excellent sensitivity with revelation to acetone gas with various concentrations from 10 ppm to 120 ppm. Furthermore, the sensor exhibited excellent selectivity toward acetone against various interfering gases. The simulation results were further verified by comparing them with fabricated sensors by Chen et al. There was a strong correlation between the simulated and real sensor results, demonstrating superior sensitivity at room temperature. Thus, before going through the fabrication process, the sensor model that was obtained could be utilized for predicting how different gas sensors would behave.

articleTitle: Fabrication Feasible Photonic Crystal Fiber for Improved THz Wave Guidance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In this work, for efficient Terahertz (THz) wave propagation a symmetrical sectored core cladding structured photonic crystal fiber (PCF) has been introduced. Comsol Multiphysics has been utilized for numerical analysis of different optical properties where finite element method has been used as a solver. The proposed PCF structure shows elevated functions in the most of the evidential optical properties’ cases because of proper geometrical specifications, and core cladding selection as well as right optimization. It shows ultra-low Effective Material Loss (EML) of 0.022 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 0.9 THz. Additionally other significant guiding optical properties have been observed and improved performances are achieved than the existing works in this literature. Moreover, fabrication feasibility has also been discussed in details.

articleTitle: An Ensemble-based Machine Learning Approach for Botnet-Based DDoS Attack Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: In the realm of Software-Defined Networking (SDN), where network dynamics evolve rapidly, safeguarding against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks remains paramount. This research introduces a novel machine learningdriven approach designed to fortify network security by effectively identifying botnet-based DDoS attacks. This approach uses an ensemble-based Random Forest classifier in conjunction with feature selection, data preparation, and other methodologies. To identify the most significant features supporting attack detection, the feature selection makes use of cutting-edge methodologies including principal component analysis, mutual information, and correlation analysis. Performance evaluation is conducted using a comprehensive set of metrics, which includes recall, precision, accuracy, and F1 measure. Notably, this model excels in addressing class imbalance, elevating its effectiveness by deploying the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to harmonize dataset disparities. Empirical findings underscore the model's proficiency, delivering high-fidelity detection of botnet-driven DDoS attacks in an SDN environment as evidenced by elevated accuracy and balanced accuracy scores.

articleTitle: Deep Clustering of Electronic Health Records Tabular Data for Clinical Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: Machine learning applications are widespread due to straightforward supervised learning of known data labels. Many data samples in real-world scenarios, including medicine, are unlabeled because data annotation can be time-consuming and error-prone. The application and evaluation of unsupervised clustering methods are not trivial and are limited to traditional methods (e.g., k-means) when clinicians demand deeper insights into patient data beyond classification accuracy. The contribution of this paper is three-fold: 1) to introduce a patient stratification strategy based on a clinical variable instead of a diagnostic label, 2) to evaluate clustering performance using within-cluster homogeneity and between-cluster statistical difference, and 3) to compare widely used traditional clustering algorithms (e.g., k-means) with a state-of-the-art deep learning solution for clustering tabular data. The deep clustering method achieves superior within-cluster homogeneity and between-cluster separation compared to k-means and identifies three statistically distinct and clinically interpretable high blood pressure patient clusters. The proposed clustering strategy and evaluation metrics will facilitate the stratification of large patient cohorts in health science research without requiring explicit diagnostic labels.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Key Sharing Mechanism for IoT Device-to-Device (D2D) Secure Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Telecommunications and Photonics (ICTP)
abstract: The advent of the Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized how physical objects in various environments connect and share information over the Internet, ushering in an era of ubiquitous data accessibility. This technology has rapidly gained popularity across diverse sectors, including education, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, etc. However, with the proliferation of IoT devices and the sensitive nature of the data they handle, the primary concern is ensuring robust data security to thwart potential misuse by malicious users. The challenge of securing IoT applications is particularly challenging due to the multifaceted demands of this technology. While traditional centralized approaches to communication provide a level of security, they often entail inherent vulnerabilities. IoT devices, constrained by limited computing power, memory, and energy resources, necessitate a more innovative approach to provide secure communication. This article presents a blockchain-based key-sharing mechanism for enhancing device-to-device (D2D) secure communication, specifically designed to address the intricacies of D2D communication without central intermediaries. This novel approach securely stores all device identifiers (IDs) and public keys on a decentralized, distributed, immutable blockchain ledger. This architecture renders tampering with blockchain records computationally infeasible for potential attackers, ensuring the integrity and availability of shared keys. Based on comprehensive simulations, experimental evaluations demonstrate the feasibility and viability of implementing blockchain-based key sharing in real-world IoT applications and services. Importantly, this approach upholds stringent security requirements while leveraging existing hard-ware, software, network infrastructure, and internet technologies, corroborating its readiness for practical deployment. In essence, this study underscores the transformative potential of blockchain in fortifying IoT device-to-device communication, paving the way for a future where secure, decentralized, and efficient data sharing among IoT devices becomes the new standard.
